Since SSH to nodes conflicts with the codebase's architecture rule against reaching nodes directly, I'm working out that zfs send/recv needs to go through a new node-agent endpoint — the primary streams zfs send output as the request body while the agent pipes it into zfs receive on an allowlisted dataset, keeping things token-authenticated and consistent with the existing narrow-endpoint design.

For VM creation on the target, the Proxmox API lets me attach an existing zvol by referencing its volid (storage:vm-x-disk-y syntax) rather than creating a new one, but the volume name must match the new VM's id or Proxmox will reject it as owned by another VM — so the received dataset needs to be named using the new VM's id from the start.

I also need to handle the cloud-init drive attachment, support incremental receives using the base snapshot sent in pass one, and add cleanup/rollback endpoints on the agent for listing and destroying these zfs snapshots with a strict dataset name allowlist.

The pool free-space check can reuse the existing Proxmox storage status API, no new agent endpoint needed there. So the agent really just needs three new routes: a streaming receive endpoint, a dataset lookup, and a dataset/snapshot delete — and since node-agent/index.js isn't clearly owned by anyone else, I'll claim it and plan for how its deployment to nodes gets rolled out.

I'm weighing piping zfs send directly over SSH versus going through the agent — SSH is simpler and works today but breaks the narrow trust model the architecture rule establishes. I'll stick with the agent-based approach as primary, possibly with an SSH fallback transport toggle since I can't push agent updates to other nodes myself.

Still, the rehearsal itself is risky: it needs a real VM on the primary node, which is strained (6G RAM available, root disk at 98%). I'm checking whether the ZFS clone landing on the data pool (114G free) rather than root makes that part safe enough.

Given the time and complexity, I should be realistic about scope and actually start building the engine: adding new job types and a VmMove model to the schema to track phase, status, plan, logs, checkpoints, and related metadata for the migration.

I'm also laying out the module structure — a types file for phases and payloads, a pure planning module for capacity math, candidate ranking, VMID allocation, phase state transitions, re-IP planning, and target config building, and a preflight module that queries the DB, Proxmox, and OVH to assemble a real MovePlan, checking capacity, VMID uniqueness across nodes, dedicated IP destination moves, agent health, and ZFS pool naming.

Now I'm sketching the IP move step (moving the dedicated IP via OVH's API and polling until the task completes, creating a vMAC on the target and removing it from the source, with rollback logic to move back), a transport module for ZFS send/recv over the agent with an SSH fallback, and a server action for requesting a VM move with dry-run support.

I'm also planning out the rest of the pieces: move candidate listing, status/cleanup/rollback actions, a phase-machine worker handler with checkpoints persisted for idempotency, and new node-agent endpoints to support ZFS send/recv in both directions so moves work between any two non-primary nodes, plus accompanying docs.

For snapshotting, I'm weighing crash-consistent `zfs snapshot` calls against using Proxmox's API snapshot feature, which can trigger a guest-agent fs-freeze for cleaner consistency when the agent is enabled.

For the final migration pass with the VM stopped, a plain local zfs snapshot suffices since no fsfreeze is needed. Using PVE's API for snapshotting complicates things since it writes into the VM's config snapshot section, which I don't want copied when building the fresh target config—so I'll need to clean those up on the source after the move.

So the plan is: pass 1 uses a PVE API snapshot named `nxmove1` for consistency, pass 2 (stopped) uses a direct zfs snapshot `nxmove2`, and after receiving both on the target I destroy them there too for a clean result. I also need to handle the cloud-init disk separately by recreating it on target rather than transferring it, and add a preflight check that refuses to move VMs with extra disks beyond scsi0 and cloudinit, for safety's sake.

Since cc_set_passwords only runs once per instance, the cipassword just travels with the disk's shadow file anyway. The instance-id Proxmox generates is likely derived from a hash of the cloud-init config data, so a changed network config would produce a new instance-id and trigger per-instance modules to rerun—reapplying the same password harmlessly, though I'm uncertain whether SSH host key regeneration would also be triggered.

Actually `ssh_deletekeys` defaults to true on new instances, so a new instance-id would delete and regenerate SSH host keys, causing visible "host identification changed" warnings for users. Worse, any vendor runcmd snippet would also rerun, potentially re-executing setup scripts that could overwrite existing game installations—though this risk may already exist today whenever ipconfig0 changes trigger a restart, so I want to verify exactly how PVE computes the instance-id.

I recall that the nocloud meta-data instance-id is generated as a sha1 hash of the user-data and network-data combined, meaning any change to network configuration would alter the instance-id and trigger this same cascade of effects.

Given that, a move causing network changes would re-run cloud-init's per-instance modules — password resets, possible SSH host key regeneration, and reruns of runcmd including the vendor snippet's `nxeon-setup.sh` call. That script reinstalling the game setup should be safe since those scripts are built to be idempotent, but it's still a risk worth flagging: both NAT-to-NAT moves with private IP changes and dedicated-IP moves with gateway changes would alter network data and trigger a new instance-id.

One mitigation is swapping in a minimal post-move vendor snippet on the target that only handles qemu-guest-agent and sshd config, excluding the setup runcmd entirely so a re-trigger is harmless aside from cosmetic password resets and host key regeneration — and I'm considering whether adding `ssh_deletekeys: false` in that vendor snippet would properly merge with user-data to prevent key regen.

PVE just derives hostname from the VM name in user-data, so that's unaffected by the clone. For networking, I need to check whether cloud-init reapplies netplan config on every boot or only on first boot — by default NoCloud's network update events are set to BOOT_NEW_INSTANCE only, meaning network config typically isn't reapplied on subsequent boots unless that policy is overridden.

But since the instance-id is a hash of the user-data and network-config, any change to ipconfig0 produces a new instance-id, which triggers BOOT_NEW_INSTANCE and causes the network config to reapply — matching the common experience that changing ipconfig0 and rebooting works. One concern is the chpasswd directive: since it re-applies the original password hash on every instance change, it would silently reset any password the customer had manually changed in-guest, so I need to flag that as a side effect to handle carefully.

Other nodes already host dedicated-IP VMs on vmbr0, so the node firewall should already permit that bridged traffic fine. For NAT, port forwards are keyed by globally-unique public ports in the DB, so after updating the server's node/IP/SSH port, syncPortForwards can reuse the same public port numbers on the target node without collision risk.

For SSH, since sshPort is also globally unique and the per-node range is identical, I can keep the same SSH port too — customers would just see a new public IP, not new ports. I'm debating whether to add a new "MOVING" status enum or just leave Server.status alone and rely on something like a provisioningStep message instead, since adding a new status risks breaking UI logic elsewhere — leaning toward keeping status untouched and just showing the customer a transitional message.

Then I realize there's a real danger: the recovery sweep auto-restarts any RUNNING server whose VM isn't actually running, so if the source gets stopped mid-move while still marked RUNNING, the sweep could bring the source VM back up unexpectedly. I need to either patch the sweep to skip servers with an active move, or simply flip Server.status to STOPPED during the cutover window and restore it to RUNNING afterward, which avoids touching another file.

Actually that STOPPED status approach is fine since the VM genuinely is stopped then — and if the customer clicks Start, the per-server job lock means the START job just queues behind the VM_MOVE job and runs safely on the new node once the move completes.

Next I'm sequencing the second snapshot and incremental send on the stopped source, then building the target VM via the API, pointing config at the received disk, and writing the move-safe snippet through the agent. For networking, I'm leaning toward keeping the same MAC address across hosts since MAC uniqueness only matters per-bridge — and preserving it avoids breaking Ubuntu's netplan cloud-init matching, which keys off MAC address.

I need to think through rollback carefully since OVH removes the vMAC association when an IP moves — so on rollback I'd recreate the source vMAC, which gets a new random MAC, meaning I also have to update the source net0 config before restarting it. After that comes starting the target and verifying guest agent/SSH reachability, then finally committing the DB with the updated node, vmid, IP, and SSH port.

I also need to make sure port-forward sync happens for both nodes, trigger the game DNS sync job, handle customer notification if the address changed, and critically set onboot=0 on the stopped source VM so it never ghost-starts after a node reboot — tagging it for cleanup and leaving the old snapshot in place for now. Cleanup of the source VM itself becomes a separate deferred job guarded against vmid/nodeId reuse.

For rollback, if anything before commit fails, I destroy the target VM/dataset, remove the target snippet, restore the source's IP/vMAC/net0 and restart it if needed, and mark the Server and VmMove records back to a failed/rolled-back state — rollback itself being best-effort and fully logged. I should favor a low zstd level with nice/ionice instead of bothering with bandwidth-limiting tools like `pv` that may not be installed. I also need to check the agent's HTTP server timeout settings, since Node's default requestTimeout could cut off a long-running stream.

Since the agent still needs to be deployed on nodes before it can handle this transport, I should build an SSH-based fallback alongside the agent-based one—defining a shared `ZfsHost` interface with both `agentZfsHost` and `sshZfsHost` implementations so the rehearsal can proceed without waiting on agent rollout.

I'm also noting vzdump as a rejected alternative given its downtime and copy-time cost, and planning how to resolve the pool/dataset path for a storage target via the API, plus a capacity preflight check comparing available node RAM against the planned requirement.

For storage, I need to confirm available space accounts for sparse zvols by checking actual used/refer bytes via zfs list, not just volsize. I'm also sketching the server-side preflight: no attached volumes, no in-flight jobs, valid status/vmid, simple config (scsi0 + cloudinit only), and confirming that existing snapshots don't interfere since the migration only sends the current snapshot state.

I'm working out where to add the ZFS host seam, deciding to expose minimal functions like agentZfsRecvStream and agentZfsSendStream from node-agent.ts so vm-move/zfs-host.ts can reuse the same agent request pattern instead of duplicating it.

I'm sketching the ZfsHost interface with list, snapshot, destroySnapshot, destroyDataset, listSnapshots, sendStream, and recvStream methods, then designing the local implementation to pipe zfs send through zstd compression and zfs receive with force/no-mount flags for incremental rollbacks, while the agent-backed implementation exposes the same operations over HTTP endpoints for streaming zfs send/recv bodies.

I'm also planning safety guards so the dataset-destroy endpoint refuses to delete a disk if a live VM config still exists for that node, and considering an SSH-based fallback transport as an alternative transition mechanism.

For the actual transfer, I'm piping the source send stream into the target receive stream, with different plumbing depending on whether the target is remote (via fetch with a duplex body), local (child process stdin), or SSH (ssh child stdin). I'm also wiring up byte-counting through a PassThrough to report job progress, but I'm wary of a circular import between the worker index and the vm-move module since index imports vm-move and vm-move would need to import back from index.

I'll sidestep that by passing a progress callback into the job handler instead of importing reportJobProgress directly, since the handler is registered in index.ts's handlers map anyway. Now I need to write the zfs-host library file and the node-agent client additions for streaming endpoints, being careful about server timeout settings since Node's default request timeout could interfere with long-running transfers.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the dependencies the vm-move worker handler needs from the rest of the codebase—things like port forward syncing, guest agent waiting, SSH reachability checks, root password retrieval, IP allocation, notifications, mail sending, audit recording, and agent snippet writing.

Now I'm designing the job handler's control flow: loading the VmMove record and checking if it's already done, handling the dry-run case by just storing a plan, running preflight checks before executing, and then stepping through phases with checkpoints persisted after each one. I'm also working through the error handling logic—deciding whether a failure should trigger a rollback, how to set the final status, and whether throwing an error to let the job retry could cause idempotency issues with the rollback state.

For transient failures mid-phase, I'm leaning toward retrying rather than rolling back immediately — if attempts remain, throw to let the worker resume from checkpoints, and only roll back on the final attempt before throwing. The tricky part is getting MAX_ATTEMPTS into vm-move.ts without circular imports, so I'll likely just define a local constant there documenting the same value used by the job system.

Thinking about the actual phase timing matters more than generic retry logic: errors before STOP_SOURCE should always retry since the source is still live and nothing's impacted, errors after STOP_SOURCE but before COMMIT should trigger immediate rollback to minimize downtime, and errors during COMMIT itself should just retry since that step is idempotent. I also need to account for admins explicitly requesting a rollback.

I'm sketching how status gets managed through the move: marking the VM stopped once the source is halted so the recovery sweep doesn't interfere, flipping back to running on commit or on a restored rollback. For the actual snapshot step, I'll hit the Proxmox API's snapshot endpoint and wait on the task, since Proxmox names the underlying zvol snapshot automatically.

I need to double check the snapshot naming fits Proxmox's allowed pattern, which it does given the cuid length. For the second quiescent pass I'm leaning toward using the raw zfsHost snapshot call instead of the API so it stays outside the VM's config and doesn't complicate rollback, keeping the pass-1 API snapshot cleanup handled during the VM_MOVE_CLEANUP step since the VM is being destroyed anyway.

For rollback I'll best-effort delete the pass-1 PVE snapshot via the API. After receiving the dataset on the target with both transfer snapshots present, I plan to destroy them post-creation since Proxmox won't surface snapshots that aren't tracked in its own config, then move on to how `qm create` should reference the received zvol in the new VM's config.

Checking volume visibility, I confirm Proxmox's zfspool plugin will pick up any zvol named vm-<id>-disk-<n>, and since ours matches the target vmid ownership won't be an issue. For cloud-init I need to pass the plaintext root password from the DB so Proxmox can hash it, falling back to omitting it if none exists, and I need to remember SSH keys must be URL-encoded when posted to the config API.

The trickier part is figuring out whether the stored, already-encoded sshkeys string would get double-encoded when sent through URLSearchParams — but since the GUI itself sends it via encodeURIComponent and PVE decodes once on the server side, passing the already-encoded value through form encoding should match what Proxmox expects.

Tags, name, description, and memory/balloon settings all carry over cleanly into the target config.

The trickier issue is the NAT private IP: it needs to be claimed before commit, since CREATE_TARGET must set ipconfig0 with the new private IP before the target VM boots at START_TARGET — but claiming it early means overwriting Server.ipAddress while Server.nodeId still points to the source, which has side effects on port-forward syncing.

I'm weighing an alternative of reserving the IP within my own transaction instead of using allocateIp, but that opens a small race window where a concurrent provision could pick the same free IP since pickFreeIp only checks Server.ipAddress — I need some kind of reservation mechanism to close that gap.

Actually, allocateIp already handles this in-process: it reserves the IP in worker memory for 10 minutes, which covers the typical dark window, and I can still fall back on the database's unique constraint as a safety net for the rare collision case. I'll go with allocateIp(target.id) at CREATE_TARGET, store the result in checkpoints.targetPrivateIp, then commit it to Server.ipAddress at COMMIT, relying on the unique constraint to catch any P2002 conflict.

Dedicated servers keep their existing ipAddress and sshPort; the DedicatedIp row just gets its nodeId and virtualMac updated at COMMIT. I also need to make sure loadMoveServer includes the node relation properly.

For notifications I'll create an in-app record via db.notification.create and only send an email through sendMail if the address changed due to NAT, using a short honest plain HTML template with no provider mentioned. I also want to call recordAudit for the server.vm_move action, but I'm realizing that function relies on impersonating() which reads cookies — something that won't work the same way inside a background worker.

Since the worker has no request context, cookies() would throw outside request scope, so I should skip impersonating() and write directly to db.auditLog.create instead. I'll track progress via progress(job.id, pct, step), reset onboot to 0 after COMMIT since the pending config change applies immediately to a stopped VM, tag the source with nxeon-moved, and set keepSourceUntil to now plus VM_MOVE_KEEP_SOURCE_DAYS (default 7 days). For the cleanup job, I'll load the VmMove record with status DONE, verify the Server's vmid and nodeId match the target and that the target VM is actually running via the API, then destroy the source VM.

The cleanup also needs to be idempotent on the source connection: delete the source snippet, release the dedicated source vMAC, remove any leftover target snapshots (nxmove1/2), then mark status CLEANED with sourceCleanedAt set—refusing to proceed if keepSourceUntil is still in the future unless forced. # VM move engine — `VM_MOVE` / `VM_MOVE_CLEANUP`

Move one server's VM from one physical Proxmox node to another, with the
customer's public address carried over when it is a dedicated IP, a few
minutes of downtime, and the source kept STOPPED (never destroyed) until an
explicit, separate cleanup. Built 2026-10-01 for the primary offload
(`docs/PRIMARY-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md`); general enough for any node→node move.

Code: `lib/vm-move/{types,plan,preflight,zfs-host,ovh-ip-move,candidates,actions}.ts`,
`worker/vm-move.ts`, node-agent v2 endpoints in `node-agent/index.js`,
schema `VmMove` + `JobType.VM_MOVE/VM_MOVE_CLEANUP`, tests in
`test/vm-move-plan.test.ts`.

## Interface for the admin ops UI

All in `lib/vm-move/actions.ts` (`"use server"`, gated by `requireArea("fleet")`,
audited via `recordAudit`). The web app never touches Proxmox/ZFS/OVH — every
mutation enqueues a `Job` the worker executes.

| Action | What it does | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requestVmMove({ serverId, targetNodeId, dryRun?, reason?, allowDropSnapshots? })` | Creates a `VmMove` row + a `VM_MOVE` job (payload `{ vmMoveId }`). `dryRun: true` runs preflight only and leaves the row `PLANNED` with the plan attached. Refused if any job/move is in flight for the server (per-server advisory lock, same as every other server action). | `{ ok, vmMoveId, jobId }` or `{ ok:false, error }` |
| `previewVmMove(serverId, targetNodeId, allowDropSnapshots?)` | Read-only preflight, no row, no job — for a live "what would happen" panel. Slow-ish (talks to both nodes, the source ZFS and OVH): ~2–8 s. | `{ ok, plan }` |
| `getVmMove(vmMoveId)` | The row incl. `plan` (MovePlan), `checkpoints`, `log` (append-only `{at,phase,msg}[]`), `phase`, `status`. Poll this while a move runs. | `VmMove & { server }` |
| `listVmMoves({ serverId?, limit? })` | Newest first. | `VmMove[]` |
| `listMoveCandidates(nodeId, realUsageByVmid?)` | Every server on a node, classified A/B/C and ranked by relief/risk (`lib/vm-move/plan.ts` `rankMoveCandidates`). Pass `{ [vmid]: { rssMB, cpuPct } }` when the caller has real per-VM numbers; plan RAM is the fallback. | `MoveCandidate[]` |
| `requestVmMoveRollback(vmMoveId)` | Flags a RUNNING, not-yet-committed move; the worker rolls back at its next phase boundary. Refused once `checkpoints.committedAt` exists. | `{ ok, jobId }` |
| `requestVmMoveCleanup(vmMoveId, { force? })` | Enqueues `VM_MOVE_CLEANUP` for a `DONE` move. Refused before `keepSourceUntil` (default 7 days, `VM_MOVE_KEEP_SOURCE_DAYS`) unless `force`. | `{ ok, jobId }` |

Job payloads: `VM_MOVE` → `{ vmMoveId }`; `VM_MOVE_CLEANUP` → `{ vmMoveId, force? }`.
Both are server-scoped (`Job.serverId`), so the worker's per-server lock keeps a
customer's START/STOP/DELETE queued behind a running move. `Job.progress` /
`Job.step` are updated live ("Full copy: 12.40 GB sent").

`VmMove.status`: `PLANNED` (dry run done) → `RUNNING` → `DONE` → `CLEANED`;
or `ROLLED_BACK` (source running again, target removed) / `FAILED` (rollback
incomplete or preflight failed — `error` says what). `VmMove.phase` is the
phase currently executing (see below). `addressChanged` is true only for a NAT
move (public IP changed) — the only case a customer email is sent.

## What a move does, phase by phase

| Phase | Source | Target | Reversible? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PREFLIGHT` | read config, snapshots, ZFS `used` | capacity (REAL avail RAM, committed RAM, pool free), agent v2 health, fleet-wide vmid scan, dataset free; OVH IP-move destinations for a dedicated IP | n/a — a dry run stops here |
| `SNAPSHOT_LIVE` | Proxmox snapshot `nxmove1-<id>` (guest-agent fs-freeze, disk only) | — | yes |
| `SEND_FULL` | `zfs send -L -e @nxmove1` → zstd | `zfs receive -F -u <pool>/vm-<newid>-disk-0` | yes (dataset destroyed) |
| `STOP_SOURCE` | graceful shutdown (90 s) then stop; `Server.status=STOPPED` | — | yes — **dark window opens** |
| `SEND_INCREMENTAL` | zfs snapshot `nxmove2-<id>`, `zfs send -i` | receive | yes |
| `CREATE_TARGET` | — | move-safe vendor snippet written; `POST /nodes/x/qemu` with the carried config, `scsi0=<storage>:vm-<newid>-disk-0`, fresh cloud-init drive, re-IP'd `ipconfig0`; engine snapshots dropped from the received dataset | yes (VM destroyed) |
| `MOVE_IP` (dedicated only) | — | OVH `POST /ip/{ip}/move {to}` + poll task; new Virtual MAC on the target service; target `net0` rewritten | yes (moved back + source vMAC recreated) |
| `START_TARGET` | — | start; guest agent (240 s); SSH banner on the dedicated IP | yes |
| `COMMIT` | `onboot=0`, tag `nxeon-moved` | — | **no** — DB cutover (`Server.nodeId/vmid/ipAddress`, `DedicatedIp.nodeId/virtualMac`), `Server.status=RUNNING`, NAT reconciled on every node, external SSH probe for NAT, `SYNC_GAME_DNS` queued if a subdomain exists, customer notice, `AuditLog server.vm_move`, `keepSourceUntil` set |

Failure policy (`worker/vm-move.ts`): before `STOP_SOURCE` a failure re-queues
the job and the retry **resumes** from the last checkpoint (nothing is
re-streamed); between `STOP_SOURCE` and `COMMIT` a failure **rolls back
immediately** (`rollbackSteps()` undoes exactly what the checkpoints say exists,
IP first) to keep the customer's downtime short; from `COMMIT` on the move is
forward-only and retries the idempotent remainder.

Resumability: every phase writes its facts to `VmMove.checkpoints`
(`liveSnapshotName`, `fullSentAt`, `sourceStoppedAt`, `incrementalSnapshotName`,
`targetVmCreated`, `ipMovedAt`, `targetVirtualMac`, `targetVerified`,
`committedAt`, …). `nextPhase()` picks the first incomplete phase; every phase
checks the world before acting (dataset already holds the snapshot? VM already
exists? IP already routed?).

## Transfer method — why ZFS send/receive

Evaluated on PVE 9.2 with real numbers from the fleet (2026-10-01):

| Option | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `qm remote-migrate` | **Rejected for now.** Still flagged `EXPERIMENTAL` in `qm help` on 9.2.4. Needs `VM.Migrate` (our `nxeon@pve!platform` token does not have it) plus the target's API fingerprint. `--online` is unsafe here: every VM runs `cpu: host` and the fleet mixes i7-7700K / i7-8700 / Xeon E-2136 / E-2236 — a live migration between different CPU models can crash the guest. Offline it copies the whole disk during the dark window (no incremental), so a 50 GB disk means ~15–30 min of downtime instead of ~3. |
| `vzdump` → copy → `qmrestore` | Works with the existing tooling but writes a full archive to the source's `/tank`, copies it, then restores — twice the I/O on an already-strained primary, no incremental, and the dark window covers the whole thing. Kept as the manual fallback runbook. |
| **`zfs send/receive`, two passes** | Chosen. Pass 1 streams a consistent snapshot while the VM runs; pass 2 (VM stopped) streams only the delta. Dark window ≈ shutdown + delta + boot (`estimateDurations()`: ~3–5 min for the primary's VMs). Every node is ZFS (`zfs-2.4.x`, `vmdata` = `data/vms` on the primary, `data` on node-3/4/5, `rpool/data` on node-2) and has `zstd`. |

Transport: the stream goes primary→node-agent (`POST /v1/zfs/recv`) or
node-agent→primary→node-agent (`GET /v1/zfs/send`) — the agent gained
`/v1/zfs/{dataset,snapshot,recv,send}` (v2) with the same allowlists as
`lib/vm-move/plan.ts` and a hard refusal to receive into / destroy any dataset
whose vmid has a VM config on that node. Until every node runs agent v2,
`VM_MOVE_TRANSPORT=ssh` in the worker's `.env` uses root SSH from the primary
(argv only, BatchMode) — a transition fallback, documented as such.

## Dedicated-IP carry-over (class A)

OVH failover IPs route to one dedicated server at a time and reach the VM via
a per-server Virtual MAC. `lib/vm-move/ovh-ip-move.ts`:

1. Preflight: `GET /ip/{ip}/move` lists the services the IP may move to. OVH
   only lists same-campus destinations — verified live: a Singapore IP lists
   `ns5002569`/`ns5013314`/`ns564103` and **not** `ns565008` (Beauharnois). This
   is the authoritative zone guard; `Node.region` equality and the two servers'
   `datacenter` fields (`sgp1` vs `bhs7`) are the pre-filters. A wrong-zone
   move is therefore impossible through this engine, not merely "unusable".
2. `MOVE_IP`: `POST /ip/{ip}/move {to}` → poll `GET /ip/{ip}/task/{id}` until
   `done` → `POST /dedicated/server/{target}/virtualMac` → poll until bound →
   target `net0=virtio=<mac>,bridge=vmbr0`, `ipconfig0=ip=<ip>/32,gw=<target /24>.254`.

# VM move engine — `VM_MOVE` / `VM_MOVE_CLEANUP`

Move one server's VM from one physical Proxmox node to another, with the
customer's public address carried over when it is a dedicated IP, a few
minutes of downtime, and the source kept STOPPED (never destroyed) until an
explicit, separate cleanup. Built 2026-10-01 for the primary offload
(`docs/PRIMARY-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md`); general enough for any node→node move.

Code: `lib/vm-move/{types,plan,preflight,zfs-host,ovh-ip-move,candidates,actions}.ts`,
`worker/vm-move.ts`, node-agent v2 endpoints in `node-agent/index.js`,
schema `VmMove` + `JobType.VM_MOVE/VM_MOVE_CLEANUP`, tests in
`test/vm-move-plan.test.ts`.

## Interface for the admin ops UI

All in `lib/vm-move/actions.ts` (`"use server"`, gated by `requireArea("fleet")`,
audited via `recordAudit`). The web app never touches Proxmox/ZFS/OVH — every
mutation enqueues a `Job` the worker executes.

| Action | What it does | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requestVmMove({ serverId, targetNodeId, dryRun?, reason?, allowDropSnapshots? })` | Creates a `VmMove` row + a `VM_MOVE` job (payload `{ vmMoveId }`). `dryRun: true` runs preflight only and leaves the row `PLANNED` with the plan attached. Refused if any job/move is in flight for the server (per-server advisory lock, same as every other server action). | `{ ok, vmMoveId, jobId }` or `{ ok:false, error }` |
| `previewVmMove(serverId, targetNodeId, allowDropSnapshots?)` | Read-only preflight, no row, no job — for a live "what would happen" panel. Slow-ish (talks to both nodes, the source ZFS and OVH): ~2–8 s. | `{ ok, plan }` |
| `getVmMove(vmMoveId)` | The row incl. `plan` (MovePlan), `checkpoints`, `log` (append-only `{at,phase,msg}[]`), `phase`, `status`. Poll this while a move runs. | `VmMove & { server }` |
| `listVmMoves({ serverId?, limit? })` | Newest first. | `VmMove[]` |
| `listMoveCandidates(nodeId, realUsageByVmid?)` | Every server on a node, classified A/B/C and ranked by relief/risk (`lib/vm-move/plan.ts` `rankMoveCandidates`). Pass `{ [vmid]: { rssMB, cpuPct } }` when the caller has real per-VM numbers; plan RAM is the fallback. | `MoveCandidate[]` |
| `requestVmMoveRollback(vmMoveId)` | Flags a RUNNING, not-yet-committed move; the worker rolls back at its next phase boundary. Refused once `checkpoints.committedAt` exists. | `{ ok, jobId }` |
| `requestVmMoveCleanup(vmMoveId, { force? })` | Enqueues `VM_MOVE_CLEANUP` for a `DONE` move. Refused before `keepSourceUntil` (default 7 days, `VM_MOVE_KEEP_SOURCE_DAYS`) unless `force`. | `{ ok, jobId }` |

Job payloads: `VM_MOVE` → `{ vmMoveId }`; `VM_MOVE_CLEANUP` → `{ vmMoveId, force? }`.
Both are server-scoped (`Job.serverId`), so the worker's per-server lock keeps a
customer's START/STOP/DELETE queued behind a running move. `Job.progress` /
`Job.step` are updated live ("Full copy: 12.40 GB sent").

`VmMove.status`: `PLANNED` (dry run done) → `RUNNING` → `DONE` → `CLEANED`;
or `ROLLED_BACK` (source running again, target removed) / `FAILED` (rollback
incomplete or preflight failed — `error` says what). `VmMove.phase` is the
phase currently executing (see below). `addressChanged` is true only for a NAT
move (public IP changed) — the only case a customer email is sent.

| Phase | Source | Target | Reversible? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PREFLIGHT` | read config, snapshots, ZFS `used` | capacity (REAL avail RAM, committed RAM, pool free), agent v2 health, fleet-wide vmid scan, dataset free; OVH IP-move destinations for a dedicated IP | n/a — a dry run stops here |
| `SNAPSHOT_LIVE` | Proxmox snapshot `nxmove1-<id>` (guest-agent fs-freeze, disk only) | — | yes |
| `SEND_FULL` | `zfs send -L -e @nxmove1` → zstd | `zfs receive -F -u <pool>/vm-<newid>-disk-0` | yes (dataset destroyed) |
| `STOP_SOURCE` | graceful shutdown (90 s) then stop; `Server.status=STOPPED` | — | yes — **dark window opens** |
| `SEND_INCREMENTAL` | zfs snapshot `nxmove2-<id>`, `zfs send -i` | receive | yes |
| `CREATE_TARGET` | — | move-safe vendor snippet written; `POST /nodes/x/qemu` with the carried config, `scsi0=<storage>:vm-<newid>-disk-0`, fresh cloud-init drive, re-IP'd `ipconfig0`; engine snapshots dropped from the received dataset | yes (VM destroyed) |

the job and the retry **resumes** from the last checkpoint (nothing is
re-streamed); between `STOP_SOURCE` and `COMMIT` a failure **rolls back

forward-only and retries the idempotent remainder.

`targetVmCreated`, `ipMovedAt`, `targetVirtualMac`, `targetVerified`,

checks the world before acting (dataset already holds the snapshot? VM already
exists? IP already routed?).

# Primary offload plan — vetting, candidates, batches (2026-10-01)

Goal: the primary node (`ns5002569`, OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K 8 threads, 62.6 GB,
region `sgp1`) should primarily run the Nxeon app (web, worker, Postgres, mail
NAT, staging) and stop being the busiest customer hypervisor in the fleet.
Everything below was measured read-only on 2026-10-01 06:07–06:12 UTC. Nothing
on any host was changed. The engine that executes the batches is
`docs/VM-MOVE.md`.

## 1. What the primary is actually doing

### Host

| Fact | Measured | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RAM | 62.6 GB total, **54.8 GB used, 6 GB available**; buff/cache 4 GB | starved |
| Swap | **10 GB / 10 GB full** — two 1 GB md partitions + an 8 GB ZFS zvol `data/swap` (`/dev/zd800`) | swap-on-zvol is deadlock-prone under ZFS memory pressure; full means every eviction is a page-out |
| Who is in swap | staging `next-server` 611 MB, prod `next-server` 313 MB, nxeon-mail 357 MB, kodely-app 564 MB, dst 402 MB, hosting-1 291 MB, each kvm 50–250 MB; worker `npm exec` 10 MB; Postgres backends ~2 GB total | the APP is what got paged out first |
| `vm.swappiness` | 60 | too eager for a hypervisor |
| ZFS ARC | 8.0 GB, `zfs_arc_max` = 8 GiB (already capped) | could go to 4 GiB |
| KSM | off (`/sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run = 0`) | node-2 saves ~5 GB with it on 13 similar guests |
| THP | `madvise` | fine |
| CPU | 8 threads; **33 vCPU allocated to running VMs** + app; load 12–15; `/proc/pressure/cpu some avg300 = 26 %` | CPU-saturated; memory PSI low right now (not thrashing at the instant measured, but one burst from it) |
| Root disk `/` (md3, 49 GB) | **98 % at 06:07 (1.3 GB free)**, 77 % after the main thread cleaned caches during this vetting | at 100 % Postgres crashes (happened 2026-09-27). Big resident items: `/var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg` **7.4 GB** (cloud images on the root disk), `/opt/nxeon` 4.8 GB, `/root/.claude` 4.4 GB, `/opt/nxeon-staging` 2.4 GB, Postgres 1.6 GB, 20+ agent worktrees × 300 MB |
| ZFS pool `data` (NVMe mirror, VM disks) | 358 GB, 244 GB alloc, 114 GB free, **65 % fragmentation** | ok on space, fragmented |
| `tank` (HDD) | 3.6 TB, 621 GB used | fine |

### Services (systemd, no cgroup priorities anywhere)

`nxeon-web` 1.38 GB, `nxeon-worker` 0.6 GB, `postgresql@17-main` 1.0 GB
(`shared_buffers` **128 MB** default, `work_mem` 4 MB, `effective_cache_size` 4 GB),
`nxeon-staging-web` 0.5 GB (+0.6 GB swapped), `nxeon-staging-worker` 0.26 GB,
nginx, `nxeon-terminal`, `nxeon-console-proxy`, Mailcow NAT (`nxeon-mail-nat.service`
→ VM 8000), fail2ban, postfix, PVE daemons. **None of nxeon-web / nxeon-worker /
postgresql has `CPUWeight`, `MemoryLow`, `IOWeight` or `OOMScoreAdjust` set** —
the app competes with 15 kvm processes as an equal. `deploy-staging.sh` and
`promote-production.sh` run `next build` ON this host (the real CPU spikes).
20+ agent worktrees under `/opt/nxeon-wt-*` share the box with it today.

### Guests (kvm RSS is the real cost; "plan" is what the customer bought)

| VMID | Name | Role | Plan RAM | VM `memory`/`balloon` | **kvm RSS** | CPU % | Disk | Network | Keep? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 200 | hosting-1 | shared-hosting node (company) | — | 8192/4096, 4 cores | 2.9 GB | 4 | 100 G | dedicated 51.79.226.201 (INTERNAL, whole-IP DNAT) | stay for now; movable later as class A |
| 105 | studionexis-soul | live Soul Pilates site (company) | Pro 8 GB | 8192/4096, 3 cores | 4.0 GB | 15 | 100 G | dedicated 51.79.226.200 (INTERNAL) | stay (live site, "don't experiment"); lower balloon floor |
| 9010 | coldemail-relay | relay (company) | — | 512 | 0.5 GB | 1 | 8 G | dedicated 51.79.168.98 (INTERNAL) | stay |
| **106** | nexis-app | company dev app | Standard | 4096/2048, 2 cores | 1.5 GB (+252 MB swap) | 1 | 50 G | config carries **51.79.226.215** — that IP is now terraheim's on node-3 (OVH routes it there); the DB row says STOPPED but the VM is RUNNING | **shut down** (owner confirms it is unused) |
| **110** | kodely-app | Kodely (company) | Nano | 6144/3072, **4 cores** | 2.6 GB (+564 MB swap) | 1 | 60 G | NAT 10.20.0.30; DB row says STOPPED, VM RUNNING | move to node-5 (company DNS, latency-tolerant) |
| 109 | terraria-i2ydef | customer | 2 GB | 2048/1536, 1 core | 1.4 GB | 18 | 20 G | **dedicated 51.79.181.111** | **class A** |
| 112 | mobilkit | customer VPS Starter | 2 GB | 2048/1536, 1 core | 1.4 GB | 5 | 25 G | **dedicated 15.235.171.120** | **class A** |
| 115 | bujangsmp | customer Minecraft | 4 GB | 4096/4096, 2 cores | 4.0 GB | 15 | 30 G | NAT, subdomain `bujangsmp`, term ended 2026-09-30 (auto-renew on) | class B — after renewal settles |
| 116 | valheim-4r5fjg | customer Valheim | 4 GB | 4096/2048, 2 cores | 2.1 GB | 15 | 30 G | NAT, 3 forwards | class B |
| 118 | dst-ddvzfe | customer DST | **3 GB** | **6144**/4096, 2 cores | 3.8 GB | 34 | 15 G (VM 50 G) | NAT, 1 forward | class B; VM is 2× its plan |
| 120 | blue | customer Valheim | 8 GB | 8192/4096, 3 cores | 4.6 GB | 20 | 50 G | NAT, 3 forwards | class B |
| 121 | projectzomboid-kc0kcr | customer PZ | 6 GB | 6144/4096, 2 cores | 4.0 GB | **183** | 30 G (VM 80 G) | NAT, 1 forward | class B — biggest CPU relief |
| 114 | darkeden-guard-sg | stopped | — | 8192 | 0 | 0 | 25 G | — | no Server row; archive/destroy candidate (owner) |

Customer guests: 7 VMs, 29 GB plan RAM, **21.3 GB real RSS**, 12 vCPU.
Company guests: 6 VMs (+1 stopped), 15.7 GB RSS, 20 vCPU. The app ≈ 4 GB.

### Hypervisor/DB drift found while vetting (not fixed — report)

- VM 106 and 110 are RUNNING on Proxmox while their `Server` rows say STOPPED.
- VM 106's `ipconfig0` is a customer's dedicated IP (terraheim, node-3). It cannot receive traffic (OVH routes the IP to node-3's Virtual MAC) but the config must be cleared before anyone ever starts it with that IP again.
- VM 116 `projectzomboid-kc0kcr` exists STOPPED on node-2 (fsn1) as well as RUNNING on the primary (121); `upnormal` (131 node-4 / 117 node-2 stopped) and `sausaugepro` (600 node-4 / 101 node-2 **running**) also exist twice. Those node-2 copies are leftovers from earlier re-provisions — disk only, except sausaugepro which is running on both.
- node-5 (bhs1) root disk is **96 % full** (its `backup` dir storage is on the 20 GB root).
- Dedicated IP pool: `51.79.226.215` was once a primary-block IP and now lives on node-3 — proof that OVH same-campus IP moves work in this fleet.

## 2. Where could anything go? (real numbers, all nodes)

| Node | Region | Host RAM | **Real avail** | Guest RSS | ARC | Committed / capacity (DB) | Threads / load | Pool free | Dedicated IPs | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| primary ns5002569 | sgp1 | 62.6 G | **6 G** | 36.4 G | 8 G | 46 / 55 GB | 8 / 14 | 114 G | 3 cust + 3 internal | — |
| node-4 ns564103 | sgp1 | 64 G | **9.2 G** | 43.1 G | 8 G | **52 / 55 GB (95 %)** | 8 / 3.4 | 195 G | 2 | ok |
| node-3 nxeon-sgp2 | sgp1 | **31 G** | **3.0 G** | 18.3 G | 8 G | **28 / 23 GB (120 %)** | 12 / 0.7 | 768 G | 4 | ok |
| node-2 nxeon-fsn1 | fsn1 (DE) | 64 G | 15.3 G | 40.3 G | 0.4 G, KSM saves 5 G | 58 / 55 GB (105 %) | 12 / 0.4 | 337 G | 1 | ok |
| node-5 nxeon-bhs1 | bhs1 (CA) | 64 G | **26 G** | 9.9 G (+ a live QA sweep) | 8 G | 8 / 55 GB | 12 / 1.3 | 400 G | 0 (1 free) | ok; root disk 96 % |

After right-sizing ARC on the two SG nodes from 8 GiB to 3 GiB (`zfs_arc_max`):
node-4 ≈ **14 GB** real avail, node-3 ≈ **8 GB**. But both are already at or past
their **committed** ceiling (`Node.capacityRamMB`, the platform's own promise):
node-4 has 2.7 GB of committed room, node-3 has none. The engine's preflight
blocks a move that exceeds the target's committed capacity
(`VM_MOVE_COMMITTED_MAX_PCT`, default 100 %), on purpose.

**Plain answer: Singapore has room for exactly the two small dedicated-IP
servers (terraria + mobilkit, 4 GB plan / 2.8 GB RSS) on node-4, and nothing
else.** The six NAT game servers on the primary (25 GB plan, 18.5 GB RSS,
11 vCPU) have no Singapore home. node-5 (bhs1) has 26 GB spare and an empty
committed ledger, but it is in Canada: every one of those six is a game
server whose players chose Singapore — a 180–220 ms RTT move is a
customer-visible downgrade, not an offload, and must not be done without the
customer's consent. node-2 (DE) is both far and over-committed.
**The owner needs another Singapore node** (a 64 GB class box like node-4
takes all six with ~25 GB to spare for growth). Alternatives that avoid a
new node only buy ~7 GB on the primary (see §4) — real relief, not enough to
change the picture.

## 3. Candidate ranking (engine classes; `rankMoveCandidates()`)

| # | VM | Class | Target | Relief (RSS / vCPU) | Downtime (est.) | Customer-visible | Risk notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 121 projectzomboid-kc0kcr | B | **new SG node** | 4.0 GB / 2 (and ~1.8 cores of real CPU) | ~4 min | new public IP, same ports (notice) | 30 GB used; PZ restarts cleanly |
| 2 | 120 blue | B | new SG node | 4.6 GB / 3 | ~5 min | new IP, same 3 forwards | 50 GB disk → longer full pass (source stays up) |
| 3 | 118 dst-ddvzfe | B | new SG node | 3.8 GB / 2 | ~3 min | new IP | right-size VM 6144→3072 at the same time (plan is 3 GB) |
| 4 | 115 bujangsmp | B | new SG node | 4.0 GB / 2 | ~3 min | **none for players** (subdomain repointed via `SYNC_GAME_DNS`) | term ended 2026-09-30 — wait for the renewal to land |
| 5 | 116 valheim-4r5fjg | B | new SG node | 2.1 GB / 2 | ~3 min | new IP, same 3 forwards | — |
| 6 | 109 terraria-i2ydef | **A** | **node-4 now** | 1.4 GB / 1 | ~3 min | **none** (IP travels) | first dedicated-IP move — do this one in the rehearsal batch |
| 7 | 112 mobilkit | **A** | **node-4 now** | 1.4 GB / 1 | ~3 min | **none** | VPS, not a game; customer may run sshd on a custom port — `guestSshPort` honoured |
| — | 110 kodely-app | B (company) | node-5 | 2.6 GB / 4 | ~4 min | Kodely's DNS A record → node-5 IP (ours) | company-owned; do early |
| — | 106 nexis-app | — | shut down | 1.5 GB / 2 | — | none (dead IP) | owner confirms |
| C | 105, 200, 8000, 9010 | C | stay | — | — | — | hosting-1 is a future class-A candidate |

## 4. Batches

**Batch 0 — host quick wins, no VM moves, no downtime** (owner runs; see §5):
cgroup priorities for the app, swappiness 10, zram instead of the zvol swap,
ARC 8→4 GiB on the primary and 8→3 GiB on node-3/node-4, KSM on (gentle),
cloud images off the root disk, nexis-app shut down, kodely-app's 4 cores → 2.
Relief ≈ 4 GB ARC + 1.5 GB nexis + ~3 GB KSM + 10 GB of swap that stops
living on ZFS; the app stops being paged out first.

**Batch 1 — rehearsal + class A to node-4** (engine, after ARC on node-4 is
capped): the throwaway rehearsal VM (see §6), then 109 terraria-i2ydef, then
112 mobilkit. Target node-4 ends at ≈ 56/55 GB committed (102 %) — set
`VM_MOVE_COMMITTED_MAX_PCT=105` for exactly these two or accept node-3 for
mobilkit with ARC capped (node-3 is 120 % committed, so no). Relief on the
primary: 2.8 GB RSS, 2 vCPU, two fewer Virtual MACs. Downtime ≈ 3 min each,
no address change, rollback = IP moved back + source started.

**Batch 2 — company off-load** (engine, class B): 110 kodely-app → node-5;
update Kodely's DNS to node-5's IP after `COMMIT`. Relief 2.6 GB RSS, 4 vCPU.

**Batch 3 — the six NAT game servers → the new Singapore node** (engine,
class B), in the order of §3, one at a time, evenings SGT, each preceded by
the in-app notice the engine sends at `COMMIT`. Relief ≈ 18.5 GB RSS, 11 vCPU.
After batch 3 the primary carries the app + mail + hosting-1 + Soul Pilates
+ relay: ≈ 12 GB guests, 16 GB total, 40+ GB free — the stated goal.

**Batch 4 (optional)** — 200 hosting-1 as class A to the new node once the
shared-hosting product's node-agent/DNAT model is reviewed (its IP is reached
by whole-IP DNAT, not a Virtual MAC — the engine refuses INTERNAL IPs today).

Rollback for every batch: the engine's own (`rollbackSteps()`), plus the
source VM kept STOPPED for 7 days (`VM_MOVE_CLEANUP` is explicit).

## 5. Does the app need more resources? Ranked answer

1. **Give the app priority over guests (today, zero downtime).** systemd drop-ins:
   ```
   # /etc/systemd/system/nxeon-web.service.d/10-priority.conf  (same for nxeon-worker; postgresql@17-main gets MemoryLow=2G)
   [Service]
   CPUWeight=800
   IOWeight=800
   MemoryLow=1536M
   OOMScoreAdjust=-800
   ```
   `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl set-property --runtime nxeon-web.service CPUWeight=800 MemoryLow=1536M` applies live without a restart; also `systemctl set-property qemu.slice CPUWeight=100` (the default — it just makes the ratio explicit) and `CPUWeight=20 MemoryLow=0 Nice=10` for `nxeon-staging-*`.
2. **Stop swapping the app out.** `sysctl -w vm.swappiness=10` (+ `/etc/sysctl.d/90-nxeon.conf`), then replace the zvol swap: `apt install zram-tools; printf 'ALGO=zstd\nPERCENT=15\n' > /etc/default/zramswap; systemctl enable --now zramswap`, and only once RAM has been freed by batch 0/1: `swapoff /dev/zd800 && sed -i '/zd800\|data\/swap/d' /etc/fstab && zfs destroy data/swap`. free and 6 GB RAM available during this work, with the main thread's
explicit instruction to avoid big operations; cloning a VM onto it for a
rehearsal was the wrong call today. Nothing in this plan has been run against

entry = '''### 2026-10-01 — Primary offload: vetting, plan, and a node-to-node VM move engine (branch `feature/vm-node-migration`, NOT promoted)

The primary (`ns5002569`) was measured read-only: 6 GB of 62.6 GB really available, swap 10/10 GB full
(8 GB of it a ZFS zvol, `data/swap`), both `next-server` processes partly paged out, 33 vCPU on 8
threads, no cgroup priority on any app unit, Postgres at `shared_buffers=128MB`, root disk at 98 %
(7.4 GB of cloud images under `/var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg`). Every other node was measured the same
way. The full vetting, the per-VM candidate ranking, the batches and the ranked "does the app need more
resources" answer are in **`docs/PRIMARY-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md`**. The plain conclusion: after right-sizing
ARC on node-3/node-4, Singapore has room for exactly the two small dedicated-IP servers on the primary
(terraria-i2ydef, mobilkit → node-4); the six NAT game servers (18.5 GB RSS, 11 vCPU) need **another
Singapore node** — node-5 (Canada) is roomy but a latency downgrade for Singapore game customers and
must not be used for them without consent.

**Engine** (`docs/VM-MOVE.md`): new `JobType.VM_MOVE` / `VM_MOVE_CLEANUP` + model `VmMove` (additive;
phase-checkpointed, resumable, dry-run, per-server lock via `Job.serverId`, automatic rollback before
`COMMIT`, source VM kept STOPPED with `onboot=0` + tag `nxeon-moved` for 7 days, explicit cleanup).
Transfer = two-pass **ZFS send/receive** over zstd (consistent guest-agent snapshot while running, then
a stopped-VM incremental — dark window ≈ 3–5 min); `qm remote-migrate` rejected (still EXPERIMENTAL on
PVE 9.2, needs `VM.Migrate` the platform token lacks, `--online` unsafe across the fleet's mixed
`cpu: host` CPU models, no incremental offline) and vzdump→restore kept only as the manual fallback.
Dedicated IPs travel: OVH `GET /ip/{ip}/move` is the authoritative same-campus guard (verified live: a
Singapore IP lists the three SGP boxes and not `ns565008` in Beauharnois), then `POST /ip/{ip}/move` +
task poll + a new Virtual MAC on the target server — the LAST step before start, with rollback moving
it back. The guest boots on the target with a **move-safe vendor snippet** (`ssh_deletekeys: false`,
agent + root SSH only) because Proxmox's NoCloud instance-id changes with the network config and would
otherwise re-run the original provisioning `runcmd` and regenerate SSH host keys. Node-agent v2 gained
`/v1/zfs/{dataset,snapshot,recv,send}` (same allowlists as `lib/vm-move/plan.ts`; refuses any dataset
whose vmid has a VM config on that node; `requestTimeout: 0` for the multi-GB upload); until every
node runs v2, `VM_MOVE_TRANSPORT=ssh` is the documented transition fallback. Target vmid is
`pickMoveTargetVmid()`: strictly above every id seen on any node, in `Server`/`ServerArchive`/`VmMove`
and the target's backup archives (never a recycled id; 9000–9999 skipped). Admin interface for the ops
UI: `lib/vm-move/actions.ts` (`requestVmMove`, `previewVmMove`, `getVmMove`, `listVmMoves`,
`listMoveCandidates`, `requestVmMoveRollback`, `requestVmMoveCleanup`), all `requireArea("fleet")`
+ audited. Pure planning logic (vmid choice, capacity verdicts from REAL available RAM, candidate
classes A/B/C + ranking, phase machine, rollback inventory, target config derivation, OVH destination
guard) is covered by `test/vm-move-plan.test.ts`.

**Found while vetting (not fixed):** VMs 106 `nexis-app` and 110 `kodely-app` are RUNNING on Proxmox
while their `Server` rows say STOPPED; 106's `ipconfig0` still carries `51.79.226.215`, a customer's
dedicated IP that now lives on node-3; `projectzomboid-kc0kcr`, `upnormal` and `sausaugepro` each exist
on two nodes (node-2 leftovers, `sausaugepro` running on both); node-5's 20 GB root disk is 96 % full
(its `backup` dir storage sits on it); `bujangsmp`'s term ended 2026-09-30 with auto-renew on.

**Not done:** the rehearsal move (the primary had 1.3 GB root-disk free and 6 GB RAM during this work;
cloning a VM onto it was the wrong call today — protocol in the plan doc §6); deploying agent v2 to the
nodes; `prisma db push`; any host-level change (every quick win is given as an exact command for the owner).

**Files:** `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/vm-move/*`, `worker/vm-move.ts`, `worker/index.ts` (handler
registration), `lib/node-agent.ts` (zfs client calls), `node-agent/index.js` (v2 endpoints),
`test/vm-move-plan.test.ts`, `docs/VM-MOVE.md`, `docs/PRIMARY-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md`.

'''
s = s[:-len(footer)] + entry + footer
# Job lifecycle: mention the two new job types next to STAGING_CONTROL if a list exists
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")
EOF
grep -n "STAGING_CONTROL" docs/DOCUMENTATION.md | head -3; sed -n 1,13p ROADMAP.md

# Nxeon roadmap

Continuous-improvement backlog, highest priority first. Agents: pick the top unchecked item you can
complete end-to-end in one session, implement it, test it (build + E2E where relevant), commit, check
it off with a dated note, then stop. Add newly discovered work as new items rather than expanding
scope mid-task. **Every change must also update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit** (see
`CLAUDE.md` → "Documentation — keep it current") and run `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` if the doc
changed.

> Rewritten 2026-07-23 to reflect reality (the previous version had many shipped items still
> unchecked). The core — provisioning, billing, domains, dedicated IPv4, multi-node, console, RBAC,
> email templates, invoices — is built and deployed. Below is what remains.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.content:
Primary offload: vetting + plan, and a node-to-node VM move engine (VM_MOVE)

Measured the primary and every other node read-only (docs/PRIMARY-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md):
6 GB of 62.6 GB really available, swap 10/10 GB full (8 GB on a ZFS zvol), the
app's own next-server processes paged out, 33 vCPU on 8 threads, no cgroup
priorities on any app unit, Postgres at defaults, root disk at 98%. Singapore
has room for exactly the two dedicated-IP servers (-> node-4 after ARC
right-sizing); the six NAT game servers need another Singapore node.

Engine (docs/VM-MOVE.md):
- JobType VM_MOVE / VM_MOVE_CLEANUP + model VmMove (additive): phase-checkpointed,
  resumable, dry-run, automatic rollback before COMMIT, source kept STOPPED with
  onboot=0 for 7 days, explicit cleanup.
- Two-pass ZFS send/receive over zstd (consistent live snapshot, then a
  stopped-VM incremental) - qm remote-migrate rejected with evidence.
- Dedicated-IP carry-over via OVH GET/POST /ip/{ip}/move (same-campus guard
  verified live) + new Virtual MAC on the target, as the last reversible step.
- Move-safe cloud-init vendor snippet so the new instance-id never re-runs the
  provisioning runcmd or regenerates SSH host keys.
- node-agent v2: /v1/zfs/{dataset,snapshot,recv,send}; VM_MOVE_TRANSPORT=ssh
  transition fallback.
- Admin server actions (lib/vm-move/actions.ts) for the ops UI; pure planning
  logic covered by test/vm-move-plan.test.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
